key_insight: HJSO first trains all variables jointly, then freezes the high-dimensional block and uses reduced-space Levenberg–Marquardt to refine the low-dimensional parameters of interest more efficiently.
engineering_relevance: This is useful when a few critical design or calibration parameters matter most, but the full model is too large for expensive second-order optimization.
method: Partition parameters into a large remaining block and a small POI block.
Run joint first-order optimization over the full parameter set.
Freeze the remaining variables and apply reduced-space LM only to the POIs.
evidence_signal: Across an eigenvalue problem, inverse Bratu PINN, and 100D Black-Scholes DeepBSDE test, HJSO reached POI-error targets faster than the joint first-order baseline and improved final POI accuracy.
watch_item: The approach depends on knowing which variables are true POIs and may not help if the POIs are not well separated from the rest of the parameter space.
paper_title: Hybrid Joint-Selective Optimization: Reduced-Space Levenberg-Marquardt Refinement of Low-Dimensional Parameters of Interest
